newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Edison, Centerior Energy to merge.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Edison, Centerior Energy to merge.

text.p: Electric utilities Ohio Edison Co. and Centerior Energy Corp. said Monday they agreed to merge, forming a new holding company, in a stock-for-stock deal valued at $4.8 billion.

The merger, which the utilities said they hope to complete by the end of 1997, would create the nation's 11th largest investor-owned electric system. The deal comes amid a wave of consolidation in the increasingly competitive industry.

Ohio Edison serves parts of Ohio and its Pennsylvania Power Co. subsidiary, based in New Castle, Pa., operates in western Pennsylvania. Centerior Energy's Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co. and Toledo Edison Co. serve northern Ohio.

"The combination of our contiguous service areas is a natural. Our service areas are located within a 500-mile radius of one-half of the U.S. population," said Robert Farling, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Centerior Energy.
Centerior Energy stock rose $1.50 to $9.125 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Ohio Edison stock fell 87.5 cents to $20 on the NYSE.

Under terms of the definitive agreement, Ohio Edison shareholders will receive one share of the common stock of the new holding company, named FirstEnergy Corp., for each share of Ohio Edison stock held.
Centerior Energy shareholders will receive 0.525 share of FirstEnergy stock for each Centerior share.
The deal was valued at $4.8 billion based on Friday's closing prices.
As of June 30, the combined assets of Ohio Edison and Centerior Energy were nearly $20 billion and annual revenues totalled $5 billion.

The companies said they anticipated that the transaction would add to earnings in the first year after the completion of the merger and that savings related to the merger to total $1 billion over the first 10 years.
They said they expected to reduce the work force by 900 positions out of the companies' current total work force of approximately 11,000.
The companies said they intend to propose a plan to extend to Centerior's Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co. and Toledo Edison Co. customers a rate reduction programme similar to Ohio Edison's.

The plan would call for a freeze of Clevelend Electric and Toledo Edison rates through 2005, a rate reduction of $300 million, or about 15 percent, in 2006, and accelerated depreciation of $2 billion in fixed costs during that period.
Willard Holland, president and chief executive officer of Ohio Edison, will become chairman of the board, president and chief executive officer of FirstEnergy.
Centerior's Farling will become vice chairman of FirstEnergy.
Ohio Edison and Centerior also said they expected FirstEnergy to set a goal of reducing debt by $2.5 billion through the year 2000.

The initial annual dividend on FirstEnergy's common stock is expected to be the same as Ohio Edison's annual dividend, currently $1.50 per share, and to provide Centerior holders with about the same dividend income they now receive on Centerior shares.
